finding: For traceless B∈M4(C), B² normal iff B is normal OR B is unitarily block diagonal with two separately traceless 2×2 blocks. Consequently the packet's T2-dual holds whenever A² or B² is normal, with the other traceless matrix arbitrary. This strictly includes genuinely nonnormal and full-rank B.
proof: Because B commutes with the normal operator B², every spectral subspace E_λ of B² reduces B. On E_0, B²=0, and SVD of the off-diagonal map gives nilpotent 2×2 blocks plus zero scalars. For λ≠0 choose μ²=λ; B_λ is diagonalizable with eigenvalues ±μ. In the orthogonal decomposition ker(B_λ−μI)⊕ker(B_λ−μI)^⊥, B_λ=[[μ I_p,C],[0,−μ I_q]]. Independent unitary changes on the two subspaces make C diagonal by SVD, giving 2×2 traceless blocks [[μ,c_j],[0,−μ]] plus uncoupled scalar eigenvalues ±μ. Discard scalar 2×2 blocks and keep each genuinely nonnormal 2×2 block. In total dimension4, if there is at least one such block, at most one additional traceless 2×2 block is needed: the remaining scalar entries have total trace zero and can be paired. If none, B is normal. Conversely each traceless 2×2 block squares to a scalar by Cayley–Hamilton, so B² is normal; normal B also has normal square. Apply the self-contained normal case or Theorem 6.1 of the 10:03 proof packet.
